title: dedicated-autoscaler-tokenbucket-enhancements
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Improvements to Dedicated autoscaler token-bucket controls and fleet utilization reporting: adds smoother burst smoothing, configurable refill/credit behavior, and new metrics for utilization and queued throughput. No breaking changes to public APIs.
description:
Motivation: We observed tail-end latency spikes and imperfect burst behavior in Dedicated fleets when traffic patterns included short bursts followed by idle periods. The current token-bucket implementation allowed sudden long bursts that caused queueing and downstream timeouts. This PR introduces refinements to token-bucket smoothing, configurable refill windows, and fleet-level utilization reporting to enable safer burst control and better SLO observability.

Changes included (summary): 1) Autoscaler: token-bucket smoothing algorithm updated to use an EWMA-based refill curve with configurable half-life to avoid instantaneous credit replenishment after idle windows. 2) New parameters: tokenbucket.refill_window, tokenbucket.min_credit_retention, tokenbucket.max_burst_duration exposed in Dedicated config and console UI. 3) Enforcement: added preemption-safe checks so burst consumption will gracefully throttle without dropping inflight requests; integrated with routing fallback policies. 4) Reporting: added fleet-level metrics for tokenbucket.fill_rate, tokenbucket.available_credits, dedicated.fleet.queueing_p95 and utilization_p90. 5) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests covering edge cases (clock skew, concurrent drains), integration test simulating spike workloads, and microbenchmarks for overhead.

Why this approach: EWMA refill prevents a cold fleet from immediately building a large credit bank after idle periods, which caused bursts that exceed transient capacity. The new retention parameter ensures small continual credits are preserved for prioritized low-latency traffic. Exposing the controls allows Ops teams to tune per-customer SLAs.

Compatibility and rollout: Defaults preserve existing behavior (backwards-compatible) and are gated behind a feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.tokenbucket_v2. We performed a staged rollout: canary fleet (5% traffic) for 48h with synthetic burst tests, progressive ramp to 50% for 72h while monitoring queued requests and latency, then full rollout. Automated rollback is wired to the existing rollback hook if queueing_p95 increases > 2x or error rate increases > 0.5% relative to baseline.

Testing: unit + integration + performance harness ran in CI with initial failures on the e2e harness due to timing flakiness; fixed by introducing deterministic timer mocks in tokenbucket tests. Benchmarks show a 22% reduction in 99th p99 request queueing during synthetic burst workloads while adding <1% CPU overhead on autoscaler controllers.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks added and results recorded - [x] Feature flag gating implemented - [x] Docs updated (console and config reference) - [x] Reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams

Notes: This PR also includes minor UI wiring for the console to surface the new fields; the UI changes are behind the same feature flag and are non-breaking. Operators should tune tokenbucket.min_credit_retention for latency-sensitive customers to avoid credit starvation.
